cases.text: Trade alert: chobes sends DJ Moore to jrayay for 125 FAAB
cases.notes: A real trade written without a siren. This case was `not_a_trade` for three waves, and its note said so plainly: no siren, so `is_trade_candidate` was false and no model call happened. That was never a judgement about the message -- it is a perfectly clear alert -- it was a description of the detector, and on 2026-09-10 the league chat proved it wrong by announcing a real trade the same way. The wider rule reads a `trade alert` header with no siren, so this now reaches the model and is logged.

cases.text: 🚨🚨🚨 FAAB 🚨🚨🚨

cases.notes: Four parties, eight assets, four different asset kinds in one alert.

cases.text: 🚨 Trade Alert 🚨 Sparkplug sends Bijan Robinson to the Chairman for 200 FAAB
cases.notes: Nobody named is on the member list, but the trade is not placed in another league either -- Sparkplug and the Chairman read like nicknames nobody has registered. 2026.2 answers unclear here rather than not_a_trade, so the bot asks who is meant instead of silently dropping a real alert.

cases.text:
🚨 Trade Alert 🚨
I sent Ja'Marr Chase to mdurgin for 450 FAAB
cases.notes: A member announcing their own trade in the first person, which is how most alerts are actually written. The announcer is placed from the sender's hashed handle, so `I` names them and the trade has two parties.

cases.text:
🚨 Trade Alert 🚨
I sent Ja'Marr Chase to mdurgin for 450 FAAB
cases.notes: Case 74's text with nobody behind it: a sender whose handle was never loaded leaves `Announcer: unknown`, `I` names nobody, and one named party is not a trade. This is the pair that proves the announcer is what changed the answer, not the wording.

cases.text:
🚨 Trade Alert 🚨
mdurgin I'm sending you Ja'Marr Chase for 450 FAAB
cases.notes: Both persons in one line: `I` is the announcer and `you` is the one member the announcement names besides them, so the alert names two people after all.

cases.text:
🚨 Trade Alert 🚨
I'm sending you Ja'Marr Chase for 450 FAAB
cases.notes: A known announcer is only ever one party. `you` names nobody here -- the alert names no other member for it to mean -- so the bot has to ask who the other side is rather than guess at whoever was being addressed in the chat.

cases.text:
🚨 Trade Alert 🚨
I'm cancelling my trade with mdurgin
cases.notes: A rescission written in the first person: `I` and `my trade` name the announcer, so the two sides of the cancelled deal are known even though no T- code is given. With nothing on file to match, the registrar asks for the code -- which is also what a dry run sees, since an uncoded rescission carries no assets to validate.

cases.text:
🚨 Trade Alert 🚨
kpbowe sends Rhamondre to mdurgin for 200 FAAB
cases.notes: A player named by first name alone, which is how the chat actually writes a familiar player -- the real message that prompted this was a `1 week Rhamondre rental`. No exact name, no surname, no defense, so resolution has to read the giving party's roster to find him. The runner's synthetic league puts him on kpbowe's, and the context pack shows the model the same roster.

cases.text:
🚨 Trade Alert 🚨
kpbowe sends Stevenson to mdurgin for 200 FAAB
cases.notes: A surname two active players share. Matching surnames across the whole directory asks which team, so this is only answerable from the giver's roster -- which holds exactly one of them. The giver's roster is consulted before the whole-directory rule for precisely this reason.

cases.text:
🚨 Trade Alert 🚨
kpbowe sends Quentin to mdurgin for 200 FAAB
cases.notes: A first name on nobody's roster but the receiving team's. The giver's roster settles nothing, so the league's rosters as a whole are searched -- still a couple of hundred names rather than the directory's thousands -- and one match is an answer. This is the step that survives a roster sync that has gone stale or an announcement that has the direction backwards.

cases.text:
🚨 Trade Alert 🚨
kpbowe sends Michael to mdurgin for 300 FAAB
cases.notes: Two players on the giver's roster answer to the name, and there are two honest readings of that. The model can pass the fragment through as an ordinary trade and let resolution ask which one, or it can see both of them in the context pack and ask itself; it has answered each way on consecutive runs. Both end in the same question with nothing logged, which is what the case is for, so `alt_kind` accepts the second reading rather than making the suite a coin toss. The code path is pinned by `test_resolve.py`, with no model involved.

cases.text:
🚨 Trade Alert 🚨
chobes sends 950 FAAB to kpbowe for Michael Pittman
cases.notes: More FAAB than the payer has. The `FAAB remaining` section of the context pack is the one part of it that is a check rather than a spelling aid: an amount a team cannot cover is answered with a question, never quietly lowered to what they can afford. Everybody in the runner's synthetic league holds 900, and this asks for 950.

cases.text: kpbowe buys Quentin Johnston from mdurgin for $65 FAAB
cases.notes: The shape that started the shadow wave: no siren, no header, a buy verb and a price. `buys` moves something and `FAAB` says what pays for it, and the wider rule needs both -- either alone is half the chat.

cases.text: chobes sells Zay Flowers to kpbowe for a 3rd round pick
cases.notes: No siren, and the price is not money: `round` and `pick` are asset words too, so an alert paid in draft capital is not held out for lack of a FAAB figure. The pick itself has no player and no amount, so it is an `other` asset with the phrase copied verbatim.

cases.text: mdurgin sends Khalil Shakir to chobes as a 2 week rental, back after the Week 6 games
cases.notes: No siren on a rental. `rental` is both a verb-ish word and an asset word in the wider rule, so it satisfies the test on its own alongside `sends`. The return condition is stated, which is what keeps `validate` from asking for one.

cases.text: that trade was highway robbery, he gave up a whole rental for nothing
cases.notes: Trash talk that clears the wider detector -- `for` and `rental` are both in it -- and has to be stopped by the model. This is the case that says out loud whose job the second gate is: the detector was widened on purpose to let messages like this through rather than risk holding a real alert out.

cases.text: anyone trading a WR? I'll pay 200 FAAB for the right one
cases.notes: An offer, not an announcement: nobody is named on the other side and nothing has happened yet. It clears the detector on `for` and `FAAB`, so the `not_a_trade` verdict is doing the work.

cases.text: thanks for the draft advice last night, saved my whole season
cases.notes: A `for` sentence that is not a trade. `for` plus `draft` is exactly the pair the wider rule accepts, which makes this the cheapest false positive the detector can produce -- one model call, one silent run row, no message in the chat.
